subject: MSA/Order Form: downstream productization and feedback license reconciliation
messages:
From: Claire Jensen <claire.jensen@orionht.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redline: downstream product use / feedback license

Hi Rishi / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed. Our legal/procurement teams reviewed the MSA + Order Form and attached a set of redlines focused on IP and productization. High-level asks from our side:

- We need explicit assurance that output used in our customer-facing product (e.g., generated UI text, summaries) can be owned/attributed to Orion and sublicensed to our customers.
- No implicit right for Redwood to retrain models on our customer data or product outputs — consent required per dataset and expressly scoped.
- We can tolerate a limited feedback/telemetry license for service improvements but need retention limits, pseudonymization, and an opt-out for regulated data.

I attached the first-pass redlines (Orion-Redlines_v1.pdf). Can you confirm whether Redwood is willing to: (1) provide a customer-output assignment or explicit title to downstream product content, and (2) accept a narrow feedback license with a 90‑day telemetry retention window and an opt-out path?

Procurement is asking for a clear path to signature this quarter, so any concrete wording you can provide would help.

Thanks,
Claire Jensen
Sr. Counsel, Orion HealthTech
claire.jensen@orionht.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Claire Jensen <claire.jensen@orionht.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Apr 2028 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA redline: downstream product use / feedback license

Claire — thanks for the redlines and the clear asks. Quick thoughts from the product/legal ops side:

- Downstream product title: we're open to granting customers broad rights to use, modify, display and sublicense generated output for their applications, subject to standard representations about customer-provided content. We are uncomfortable with a blanket assignment of our model weights or any claim that the customer "owns" the model. Suggestion: a carveout clause that conveys customer rights in Generated Output (defined) but preserves Redwood ownership of the Model and Model Improvements.

- Training / retrain consent: agree in principle that retraining on customer data should be opt-in. We can add an explicit opt-in toggle in the Order Form for any data used for model retraining, and a separate set of commercial terms (e.g., credit / compensation for retrain).

- Feedback / telemetry: we can accept a narrow, non-exclusive feedback license limited to service improvement, with a 90-day retention window for telemetry and data minimization for regulated data. We will propose pseudonymization and a pathway for customers to request deletion.

I'm pasting a short proposed sentence set below to give your team something concrete to react to. If that looks good, Laura can formalize into redline language.

---- proposed bullets (informal) ----
1) "Generated Output" means content produced by Redwood's Service in response to Customer prompts. Customer shall have a perpetual, worldwide, sublicensable right to use, reproduce, distribute, and create derivative works of Generated Output for Customer's business purposes.
2) Redwood retains ownership of Models, Model weights, and Model Improvements. Customer rights under (1) do not constitute a transfer of title to Redwood's Models or Model Improvements.
3) Redwood will not use Customer Content or Generated Output to retrain Models absent Customer's explicit written opt-in; opt-in terms will be set in the Order Form.
4) Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive license to use aggregated or pseudonymized telemetry and feedback for service improvement for up to 90 days, unless Customer designates specific data as regulated or opts out via the console.

---- end proposed bullets ----

Happy to jump on a 30m call to align with procurement/legal. If Laura can draft precise redline text tomorrow, we should be able to get a reviewed counter by end of week.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com

Claire — looping in language from our side after a quick legal pass. Monica and I aligned on the key principles and drafted suggested redline wording (attached: Redline_Suggested_Wording.docx). Please see the core clauses below — these are intended to be minimal, workable, and to match the commercial intent Rishi outlined.

Proposed contract language (for insertion into §3 - License & Ownership):

3.1 Definitions: "Generated Output" means content generated by the Service in response to Customer Input. "Customer Content" means data, prompts, and materials provided by Customer or its end users.

3.2 Customer Rights in Generated Output: Subject to Customer's compliance with the Agreement, Redwood hereby grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, sublicensable right to use, reproduce, distribute, and create derivative works of Generated Output for Customer's internal and customer-facing productization (including sublicensing to Customer's end users).

3.3 Redwood Model Rights: Notwithstanding §3.2, Redwood retains exclusive ownership of the underlying Models, Model weights, and any Model Improvements. Customer shall not acquire any rights to Redwood's Models by virtue of use of Generated Output.

3.4 Training & Retrain Consent: Redwood will not use Customer Content or Generated Output to train or improve any Redwood model without Customer's explicit written consent (which can be granted via order form checkbox or separate SOW). Any such consent shall be governed by a separate schedule addressing scope, compensation, and data handling.

3.5 Feedback & Telemetry License: Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use aggregated and pseudonymized telemetry and feedback for the sole purpose of service operation, diagnostics, and product improvement. Unless otherwise agreed, Redwood will retain such telemetry for no longer than ninety (90) days and will provide a programmatic opt-out for regulated data types.

We can accept minor editorial changes from Orion, but two notes: (a) we cannot accept retroactive assignment of model improvements; (b) we need a workable opt-out mechanism (console flag + documented deletion workflow).

Next steps: if Orion confirms acceptance of the 90-day retention and the opt-in retrain mechanism, we propose a final redline exchange and a short SOW definition for any retraining engagements. Monica — can you help capture procurement timeline and whether they need any evidence (SOC2 artifacts) to move forward?

Regards,
Laura Bennett
